signature.one_line: Fly-on-the-wall call recording made readable by speaker-coded captions above the head: on-camera voice in white serif, off-camera voice in accent wide sans.
unique_devices: Two-voice caption system: on-camera speaker in white bold high-contrast serif (45 px), off-camera/phone voice in accent #EDF21C heavy wide sans (49 px) with a thin dark outline, ~5 % H higher; the style switches by hard cut when the speaker changes
Captions sit above the subject's head (centre y 16-29 % depending on framing) because the camera is high-angle and the subject sits in the lower two thirds
Result-first title stack for the first ~87 frames: 2-word heavy white serif headline over a accent rounded highlight bar stating the outcome + one emoji, over a 15-frame blur-to-sharp opening
One candid aside pill (black serif in parentheses + laughing emoji on a white rounded pill at ~73 % height), used once as a pattern interrupt
signature.why_it_works: Stating the outcome first creates a payoff to wait for; colour-coded voices make a one-angle real conversation easy to follow muted, and leaving real friction in builds trust.

hook.type: result first + in medias res (outcome title over a call already in progress)
hook.first_frame: high-angle static shot of the speaker at a desk with laptop and mug, blurred for 15 frames then sharp, white serif title + accent outcome bar in the upper quarter

structure.what: outcome title + self-aware opener that names the situation
the other party pushes back / tries to end the call; light humour
the pitch: who we are and what we offer; candid aside pill
objection about an incumbent supplier handled live
concrete answers: price, product specs, logistics
the other party agrees to a trial; next step set up; sign-off

pacing.note: picture changes rarely (longest shot ~28 % of runtime); the 3-4-word caption swaps (~1 per second) are the visual refresh

captions.what: speaker-coded phrase captions, 2-5 words, one line, no box
captions.how: on-camera voice: white serif 45 px, centred just above the head (centre y 16-29 % by framing); off-camera voice: accent wide sans 49 px with ~1.5 px dark outline at ~21 %; hard cut in ~1 frame before the first word, hard cut out

background_text.what: result-first title: 2-word white heavy serif headline
background_text.how: 99 px, centred at 15.7 % height, soft shadow; on from frame 0 under the blur-to-sharp opening; hard cut out

background_text.what: accent outcome highlight bar under the title
background_text.how: solid accent rounded bar x 11.4-88.5 %, y 19.5-25.1 %, radius ~2 % W; black heavy serif 56 px sentence + one emoji at the end

cards_lists.what: aside pill (candid parenthetical remark + laughing emoji)
cards_lists.when: once, starting at ~22 % of runtime, ~90 frames
cards_lists.how: white rounded pill x 15-85 %, y 70.5-75.3 %; black heavy serif ~46 px in parentheses; hard cut in/out

layout.how: subject in the lower two thirds, desk/laptop/mug visible; upper third left clear for captions and title

camera.how: one punch-in section to ~115 % at ~26-43 % of runtime; otherwise locked

transitions.how: 15 frames from heavy blur to sharp, power2.out, title already on

captions_spec.script: latin (English as spoken; brand names spelled correctly on screen even if mis-transcribed)

case.self: sentence case as spoken (proper nouns capitalised)

captions_spec.punctuation: commas and apostrophes kept; few full stops
captions_spec.emoji: none in captions (only in title bar and aside pill)

grouping.break: every 2-5 words; colour switches with the speaker
grouping.speaker_rule: the person on camera = white serif; the off-camera / phone voice = yellow wide sans, placed ~5 % H above the white line when both are on screen

layout.self_center_y_pct: 16-29 (sits just above the subject's head: 28.9 % in the wide high-angle shot, 26.1 % when punched in, 16.2 % in a tighter section)

self.font_class: bold transitional/modern serif (high contrast, ball terminals)

closest_match.google: Playfair Display Bold / DM Serif Display

other.font_class: heavy wide (expanded) grotesque sans with a thin dark outline
other.stroke: ~1 px dark outline at 720 (~1.5 px at 1080, estimated)

title.when: frames 0-87 at 30 fps (the opening beat), centre y 15.7 %

title_bar.box: solid yellow #EDF21C rounded rectangle x 11.4-88.5 %, y 19.5-25.1 % (5.7 % H), radius ~2 % W (estimated)
title_bar.when: frames 0-87 at 30 fps, with the title

animation.entry: hard cut, whole phrase at once, ~1 frame before the first spoken word
animation.exit: hard cut on the next phrase
animation.speaker_switch: colour/font and height change on the cut; no transition
animation.title: title + bar present from frame 0 (over a 15-frame blur-to-sharp reveal of the footage) and hard-cut out after ~87 frames

other_text_spec.when: once, starting at ~22 % of runtime, held ~90 frames
other_text_spec.text: white #FFFFFF rounded pill x 15-85 %, y 70.5-75.3 % (4.8 % H) with black heavy serif text in parentheses + one laughing emoji, e.g. '(aside text here)' (~2.1 % H ink, est. ~46 px)

style.look_intent: warm, mid-contrast, natural saturation; soft indoor daylight with beige/brown tones, slightly soft

sound.music: voice only (no bed detected); real call audio with the phone on speaker
sfx: keep natural pauses and fillers; lift the quieter phone-side voice to narrow the 7.4 LU range

sound.method: heuristic (onset-envelope beat periodicity + level in speech gaps); not a classifier

catalog_styles.role: two voices told apart by font and colour

use_when: the footage is a real recorded conversation (sales call, negotiation, customer call) with an off-camera voice
two voices must be told apart on screen without cutting to the second person
the outcome is known and can be teased as a result-first title
the camera is high-angle or the subject sits low, leaving the upper third free
avoid_when: single-voice talking head with no second party
a fast-paced, heavily cut reel is wanted (this relies on long static shots)
the subject's face fills the upper third (captions would cover it)
brand_prompt:
Use /video-pipeline with /video-captions on videos/<project>. Apply style blueprint B50 (video-reference-match/references/blueprints/B50.json) to this brand.
Canvas 1080x1920, 30 fps. All positions are % of frame; px are at 1080x1920.

BRAND TOKENS (use the brand's colour/font for each role; keep the contrast relationship: {{TEXT}} and {{ACCENT}} must each stay >= 3:1 on the footage behind the captions, and {{ACCENT_2}} >= 4.5:1 on the {{ACCENT}} bar)
- {{TEXT}}      on-camera voice captions, title          default #FFFFFF
- {{ACCENT}}    off-camera voice captions, outcome bar   default #EDF21C (yellow)
- {{ACCENT_2}}  text on the outcome bar and aside pill   default #000000
- {{SURFACE}}   not used                                 default none
- {{CARD_BG}}   aside pill fill                          default #FFFFFF
- {{FONT_DISPLAY}} on-camera voice, title, bar, pill     default Playfair Display 700/900 (bold high-contrast serif)
- {{FONT_BODY}}    off-camera voice                      default Syne 700 (heavy wide grotesque; Archivo ExtraBold Expanded is closer)
- {{HANDLE}}    not shown
- {{LOGO}}      not shown

CAPTIONS (two voices, colour-coded)
1. English as spoken, sentence case, commas/apostrophes kept; spell names and brand names correctly. No emoji in captions.
2. Grouping: 2-5 words per caption (about 3-4), one line, max line width 55 % W; the style switches whenever the speaker switches.
3. On-camera voice: {{FONT_DISPLAY}} 700 at 45 px, {{TEXT}}, no box, very soft dark shadow. Centred, sitting just above the subject's head: centre y 28.9 % in a wide high-angle shot, 26.1 % when punched in, ~16 % in a tight shot.
4. Off-camera / phone voice: {{FONT_BODY}} at 49 px, {{ACCENT}} with a thin ~1.5 px dark outline, centred at ~21 % of height (about 5 % above where the on-camera line sits when both show).
5. Animation: none. Each phrase appears by hard cut ~1 frame before its first word and is replaced by hard cut. No pop, fade or highlight.

OTHER TEXT
6. Result-first title for the first ~87 frames, over a 15-frame blur-to-sharp opening of the footage: 2-word title (e.g. "Headline here") in {{FONT_DISPLAY}} 900 at 99 px, {{TEXT}}, soft shadow, centred at 15.7 %; under it a solid {{ACCENT}} rounded bar x 11.4-88.5 %, y 19.5-25.1 % (radius ~2 % W) with the outcome in {{FONT_DISPLAY}} 900 at 56 px, {{ACCENT_2}}, ending in one emoji. Both hard-cut out together.
7. One candid aside, once, starting at ~22 % of runtime, held ~90 frames: {{CARD_BG}} rounded pill x 15-85 %, y 70.5-75.3 % with {{ACCENT_2}} heavy serif (~46 px) text in parentheses plus one laughing emoji.

EDIT DEVICES
8. Keep one high-angle static camera; jump-cut dead air between turns (about 5-6 cuts/min) and add one ~115 % punch-in section around 26-43 % of runtime. Leave real friction (rejection, objection) in.

GRADE
9. Grade from the user's footage (video-style / grade.py); target look: warm, mid-contrast, natural saturation, soft indoor daylight.

AUDIO
10. Voice only, no music bed or SFX. Master to about -14.4 LUFS, true peak <= -1 dBTP; lift the quieter phone-side voice.

VERIFY before rendering
a) Render a test frame with "KEY WORD" as an on-camera caption at 45 px centred at 26 % and as an off-camera caption at 49 px centred at 21 %, then measure:
   python video-reference-match/scripts/caption_probe.py <test.mp4> --out <dir> --at <t> --box 0.25,0.24,0.75,0.285 --ink "{{TEXT}}:60"
   python video-reference-match/scripts/caption_probe.py <test.mp4> --out <dir> --at <t> --box 0.05,0.19,0.95,0.235 --ink "{{ACCENT}}:80"
   Title: --box 0.25,0.13,0.75,0.185 --ink "{{TEXT}}:60"; bar text: --box 0.12,0.2,0.80,0.245 --ink "{{ACCENT_2}}:90".
b) Expected ink for any word: video-reference-match/scripts/fit_font.py with the token font and px above (reference ink heights: on-camera 2.19 % H, off-camera 2.03 % H, title 3.75 % H, bar 2.11 % H). Required: within ±0.5 % H of the fit_font.py value; positions within ±1 % of height; colours equal to the tokens.
